title: WHAT DO YOU HAVE IN YOUR HOUSE?
paragraphs: WHAT DO YOU HAVE IN YOUR HOUSE?
That question must have pierced her like a blade.
Because she had nothing.

Her husband was dead.
The creditors were coming.
Her sons were about to be taken as slaves.

Imagine the shame.
The panic.
The silent nights where a mother pretends to be strong while her world collapses.
She ran to the prophet Elisha and cried for help.
And he asked a strange question:

“What do you have in your house?”
— 2 Kings 4:2

Not: What do you wish you had?
Not: Who failed you?
Not: Why did this happen?
Just this:
What do you already have?
Her answer?
“Nothing… except a small jar of oil.”
Just oil.

Not land.
Not money.
Not connections.
Just one little jar.
But heaven loves starting with almost nothing.

Elisha told her to gather empty jars from her neighbors.
Not a few.
Imagine her boys knocking on doors…
“Can we borrow your empty jars?”

Confusing.
Embarrassing.
Risky.
But obedience opened the door to a miracle.

They shut the door.
She began to pour.
And the oil kept flowing.
Jar after jar after jar.
Until every empty vessel was filled.
Only when there were no more jars did the oil stop.
Listen closely, friend:
God didn’t multiply what she didn’t have.
He multiplied what she surrendered.
The miracle was waiting inside her house all along.
And the same pattern echoes through the Gospel.

A boy’s lunch becomes a feast in the hands of Jesus Christ.
Five loaves. Two fish. Thousands fed.
A sinner’s broken life becomes a testimony when laid at the cross.
Because the kingdom of God multiplies surrender.

Your small faith.
Your wounded past.
Your trembling obedience.
Place it in Christ’s hands.
And watch grace overflow.
Friend, hear the question again:
What do you have in your house?

Your talent.
Your story.
Your time.
Your tears.
It may feel small.
But surrendered to Jesus, small things become rivers of mercy.

The widow’s debt was paid.
Her sons were saved.
Her future was restored.
All from a single jar.
Because our God specializes in multiplication after surrender.
So bring your jar to Christ.

Empty.
Honest.
Unashamed.
And let Him fill it with grace that never runs dry.
